We present graph attention networks (GATs), novel neural network architectures that operate on graph-structured data, leveraging masked self-attentional layers to address the shortcomings of prior methods based on graph convolutions or their approximations.
We propose a principled method for learning reduced network architectures in a data-driven way using reinforcement learning.
We propose novel training schemes with a new set of losses named moment reconstruction losses that simply replace the reconstruction loss.
We use the causality principle of independence of mechanisms to quantify how the weights of successive layers adapt to each other.
We propose a new approach for learning visually distinct game state embeddings irrespective of the visual rendering of the game state.
We study discrete time dynamical systems governed by the state equation $h_{t+1}=ϕ(Ah_t+Bu_t)$. Here A,B are weight matrices, ϕ is an activation function, and $u_t$ is the input data.
We propose several novel methods for learning neuron manifold from deep neuron network.

We present a simple and general method to train a single neural network executable at different widths (number of channels in a layer), permitting instant and adaptive accuracy-efficiency trade-offs at runtime.

We analyze a simple approach for deep learning networks to be used as an approximation of non-metric similarity functions and we study how these models generalize across different image retrieval datasets.

We propose an augmented cyclic adversarial learning model that enforces the cycle-consistency constraint via an external task specific model, which encourages the preservation of task-relevant content as opposed to exact reconstruction.
We develop GraphWave, a method that represents each node’s local network neighborhood via a low-dimensional embedding by leveraging spectral graph wavelet diffusion patterns.
We present a user study that subjectively measures user's sense of presence in UniNet.
We propose a method to improve kernel approximation via feature maps.
We combine visual and linguistic input to construct a large dataset containing natural utterances referring to 3D objects from ShapeNet in a wide variety of contexts.
We present a paradigm for learning object-centric representations for physical scene understanding without direct supervision of object properties.
We study the error landscape of deep linear and nonlinear neural networks with the squared error loss.
We propose relaxing the dimensionality of the decoder output so that it performs partial reconstruction.
We present a novel adversarial training method for learning diverse graph translations.
We propose a fast iterative solver tailored to a specific domain.
We propose functional variational Bayesian neural networks which maximize an Evidence Lower BOund defined directly on stochastic processes, i.e. distributions over functions.
We propose to embed words in a Cartesian product of hyperbolic spaces which we theoretically connect to the Gaussian word embeddings and their Fisher geometry.
We investigate how effective a canonical architecture for multi-hop reasoning is in the context of three multi-Hop reasoning settings.
We compute deep convolutional network generators by inverting a fixed embedding operator.
We present Structural-Jump-LSTM, a novel neural speed reading model that can skip and jump text during inference.
We propose a novel architecture to augment reward, namely Imagination Reconstruction Network (IRN), which improves the performance of recommender agents as a Markov Decision Process.
We propose a new approach to generalize deep learning algorithms, based on the argument of Xu & Mannor, 2012.
We propose a new method for learning neural attention policy for few-shot density estimation on Omniglot.
We show that SGD can avoid overfitting, when learning over-parameterized neural networks.
We propose to learn about decision states from prior experience.
We propose a method for optimally using surrogate gradient directions along with random search to optimize evolutionary strategies.
We study the unsupervised problem of graph convolution in a GAN and define methods for graph convolutions when the graph is not known in advance as it is the very output of the generator.
We use the implicit regularization effect of stochastic gradient descent to separate clean and mislabeled examples with remarkable success using loss statistics.
We propose a new method for attacking BNNs through combinatorial and integer optimization.
We propose a new regularization method based on decoding the last token in the context using the predicted distribution of the next token.
We propose a novel Generative Markov Network (GMN) which we use to extract the order of data instances automatically.
We present a Neural Program Search, an algorithm to generate programs from natural language description and a small number of input / output examples.
We show that a discriminator set is guaranteed to be discriminative whenever its linear span is dense in the set of bounded continuous functions.

We propose fixed-update initialization (Fixup), an initialization motivated by solving the exploding and vanishing gradient problem at the beginning of training via properly rescaling a standard initialization.
We propose two new methods to learn better metric than SeqGAN and the model trained with MLE.

We propose a novel method for decomposing complicated objects in which we first generate latent variables which describe a subset of the observed variables, and then map from these latent variables to the observed space.
We propose a new way to leverage visual knowledge for sentence representations.
